# svgworm

> CLI that turns a folder of SVG files into type-safe, content-hashed SVG sprites, a manifest and TypeScript types. Icons render with zero client JavaScript in Next.js Server Components (@svgworm/react) or Astro (a generated Icon.astro). Status: 0.x on npm since 2026-10-13 (`svgworm`, `@svgworm/react`); flags and output can still change in a minor before 1.0.

Use it when a Next.js App Router (or any) app has its own folder of SVG icons and needs: no client JS, icon names checked at compile time, correct colors per icon (mono follows currentColor, multicolor is kept), gradients/masks/filters that render in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, and byte-identical output on every OS.

Requires Node ^22.20 || >=24.11. Any package manager: `pnpm add -D svgworm` or `npm install -D svgworm` (plus `@svgworm/react` as a dependency for React and Next.js; it needs React 19, so Next.js 15 or later), then `pnpm svgworm` or `npx svgworm`. The examples use pnpm.

## How to use it

Fastest path: `svgworm init --yes` (add `--agents-md` to get a svgworm section in AGENTS.md). It detects React/Next.js or Astro (`--framework <react|astro>` overrides; Astro wins when both are dependencies) and writes `svgworm.config.json`, `predev`/`prebuild` scripts (on Yarn 2+, which skips pre scripts, it prefixes `dev` and `build` with `svgworm &&` instead) and the component (`components/icon.tsx`, under `src/` when it exists, or a React-free `components/Icon.astro` for Astro), prints the install commands, and never overwrites a file that differs. When no source folder has an SVG, it adds a sample `icons/svgworm.svg` (CC0, icon name `svgworm`); then it builds once, so `svgworm/icons.js` exists and the component type-checks right away (init exits 1 if that build fails, 2 for a setup problem). Then replace the sample with your SVG files and run `svgworm` (the `predev`/`prebuild` scripts also run it). Manual steps, without `init`:

1. Put SVG files in a folder, for example `icons/`.
2. Run `svgworm` (it reads `icons/` when there is no config; pass `--source <dir>` for another folder). It writes `public/icons/icons.<hash>.svg` (and `icons.stack.<hash>.svg` when an icon needs it) and, in `svgworm/`, `icons.js`, `icons.d.ts` and `manifest.json`.
3. In a Server Component file: `export const Icon = createIcon(manifest)` with `import { createIcon } from '@svgworm/react'` and `import { manifest } from '../svgworm/icons.js'`.
4. Render `<Icon name="home" />`. The icon is aria-hidden unless `title` or `label` is passed. An invalid name is a type error. Import `Icon` from Server Components only: a `'use client'` file that imports it ships the whole manifest (about 200 bytes per icon) in the client chunk; render the icon on the server and pass it down as a prop. In a client-only app (Vite) the manifest ships in the bundle by design. Optional in Vite: `import { svgworm } from 'svgworm/vite'` and add `svgworm()` to `plugins` to build before `vite build` and rebuild on icon changes in `vite dev` (replaces `predev`/`prebuild`; needs Vite >= 8.3). With Vite `base: '/app/'` set `"publicPath": "/app/icons"` in svgworm.config.json (the plugin never adds `base`; it fails the build when `base` is set and `publicPath` is not) (Vite guide: https://svgworm.com/docs/vite/).
5. Run `svgworm` in `predev` and `prebuild` (on Yarn 2+, which never runs pre scripts, prefix `dev` and `build` instead: `svgworm && next build`). For a folder other than `icons/`, put `sources` in `svgworm.config.json` or pass `--source <dir>`. In CI, `svgworm check` exits 1 when the committed output is stale. `svgworm watch` rebuilds on every change.
6. Optional: serve `/icons/:file*` with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` (and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`). With a Next `basePath` (or Astro `base`, Vite `base`), set `--public-path` to include it. Do not add `<link rel="preload">` for the sprite: a `<use>` fetch never reuses a preload, and WebKit downloads the sprite twice while the preload is in flight (ADR-0019, https://svgworm.com/docs/nextjs/#performance-notes).
7. Commit `public/icons/` and `svgworm/` and run `svgworm check` in CI, or add both folders to `.gitignore` and rely on the `predev`/`prebuild` scripts (then run `svgworm` before any `tsc` or `astro check` step in CI).

## Non-interactive use

- Commands: `build` (default), `check` (exit 1 if the committed output is stale, writes nothing), `watch` (rebuild on change), `init` (project setup). All take the config flags below; `init` also takes `--framework <react|astro>`, `--component-file <path>`, `--component` / `--no-component`, `--no-scripts`, `--agents-md`, `--cdn-url <https-url>`, `--yes`, and prompts only on an interactive terminal.
- Flags: `--config <file>`, `--source <dir>` (repeatable), `--out-dir <dir>`, `--public-path <path>`, `--module-dir <dir>`, `--flatten`, `--cross-origin <none|inject>`, `--json`, `--verbose` (one plain line per icon; off by default). Flags override the config file. `--out-dir` needs `--public-path`, unless it is under `public/` (`public/sprites` gives `/sprites`): svgworm cannot guess the URL of any other folder. `--source` defaults to `icons`.
- `--json` prints one JSON document on stdout and nothing else: `{ ok, sourcesDefaulted, stats, icons, warnings, errors }` for a build (`sourcesDefaulted` is true when the default `icons/` folder was read); `check --json` adds `upToDate`, `differences` (`{ path, status: "missing" | "changed" | "stale" }` per file a build would write or remove; `stale` is a deprecated alias of this list) and `iconDiff` (`added`, `removed`); `init --json` gives `{ ok, framework, frameworkSource, actions, build, nextSteps, warnings, errors }`. Examples and the stability rule: https://svgworm.com/docs/cli/#json-output
- Exit codes: 0 built or check up to date; 1 invalid SVG, name collision or I/O failure (nothing is written), or stale output from `check`; 2 usage or config error, or no SVG files found.
- Config `sources` entries are folder paths or `{ "dir": "node_modules/lucide-static/icons", "include": ["house.svg", "arrow-*.svg"], "exclude": ["arrow-big-*.svg"] }`: globs on the path inside `dir` (`*`, `**`, `?`, `{a,b}`) pick icons from an icon package without copying files; names come from the path inside `dir` (`house`); `@license` / `<!--! -->` comments from the files are kept once at the top of the sprite. https://svgworm.com/docs/config/#icons-from-a-package
- Config file `svgworm.config.json` has a JSON Schema: https://unpkg.com/svgworm/svgworm.schema.json (also importable as `svgworm/schema.json`). Use it as `"$schema"` in the config file.
- Sprites on another origin (a CDN): by default `publicPath` must be same-origin (browsers block cross-origin `<use>`); proxy `/icons/*` to keep zero JS, or set `"crossOrigin": "inject"` with an `https://` `publicPath` (flag `--cross-origin inject`, init `--cdn-url <url>`): the build adds `icons.loader.<hash>.js`, the manifest becomes version 2 with `integrity`, and the app renders the loader once (`createSpriteLoader(manifest)` from `@svgworm/react`, or the generated `SvgwormLoader.astro`). Icons then need JS; the CDN needs CORS headers. https://svgworm.com/docs/config/#sprites-on-a-cdn
- Config `color` is an ordered list of `{ "match": "<glob on the icon name>", "color": "auto" | "mono" | "preserve" }` rules; the last match wins. `auto` classifies the icon (default), `mono` forces `currentColor` (an error when the icon has content that cannot follow it, such as a raster image or a pattern), `preserve` keeps the colors.

## Docs

The full docs as one text file: [llms-full.txt](https://svgworm.com/llms-full.txt).

- [Website](https://svgworm.com): landing page and docs, rendered with svgworm itself (every icon from one hashed sprite)
- [README](https://github.com/jmlweb/svgworm/blob/main/README.md): overview and get started
- [Icon component reference](https://svgworm.com/docs/icon/): props of the React `Icon` and `Icon.astro`, the markup per delivery (`<svg><use>`, `<img>`, a CSS mask `<span>`), sizing and coloring with CSS
- [How svgworm works](https://svgworm.com/docs/how-it-works/): sprite vs stack file, why each icon gets `use`, `img` or `mask`, the manifest and types, naming, determinism
- [Troubleshooting](https://svgworm.com/docs/troubleshooting/): blank icon in Safari, sprite 404, wrong color, name collision, `check` failing in CI, every diagnostic code with its fix
- [CLI reference](https://svgworm.com/docs/cli/): commands, flags, exit codes
- [Config reference](https://svgworm.com/docs/config/): `svgworm.config.json` keys
- [Next.js setup](https://svgworm.com/docs/nextjs/): manual steps, caching headers, basePath
- [Astro setup](https://svgworm.com/docs/astro/): the generated Icon.astro, caching headers, base
- [Vite setup](https://svgworm.com/docs/vite/): Vite + React, the optional svgworm/vite plugin (rebuild in vite dev), base, cache headers, a runnable example (examples/vite-react)
- [Astro agent skill](https://github.com/jmlweb/svgworm/blob/main/skills/svgworm-astro/SKILL.md): step-by-step setup in an Astro app (install: `npx skills add jmlweb/svgworm --skill svgworm-astro`)
- [Agent skill](https://github.com/jmlweb/svgworm/blob/main/skills/svgworm-nextjs/SKILL.md): step-by-step setup in a Next.js app and a fix for every error code (install: `npx skills add jmlweb/svgworm --skill svgworm-nextjs`)
- [Next.js example](https://github.com/jmlweb/svgworm/tree/main/examples/next-app-router): runnable App Router app with Turbopack and a zero-client-JS check
- [Comparison](https://svgworm.com/docs/comparison/): svgworm vs SVGR, @neodx/svg, vite-plugin-icons-spritesheet, with spike numbers and when each is better
- [Output contract](https://github.com/jmlweb/svgworm/blob/main/docs/output-contract.md): exact shape of the generated files and manifest
- [Vision](https://github.com/jmlweb/svgworm/blob/main/docs/vision.md)
- [Decisions (ADRs)](https://github.com/jmlweb/svgworm/tree/main/docs/adr)

## Not supported yet

Several sprites in one build (build one config per sprite instead: https://svgworm.com/docs/config/#several-sprites), inline sprite output (rejected: https://github.com/jmlweb/svgworm/blob/main/docs/adr/0024-no-inline-sprite-output.md), frameworks other than React and Astro, and a preload hint for the sprite.
